subject.title: Feature Request: Extract text from document attachments in Telegram channel

question: Should Office attachments be auto-extracted as a bundled baseline capability, supported only through external document-extractor plugins, or deferred in favor of provider-native file forwarding?
rationale: Each direction changes dependency ownership, attack surface, resource limits, and cross-channel behavior; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Shared bounded bundled extraction
options.body: Approve a narrow DOCX-first implementation in the bundled document-extract plugin with strict archive, output, timeout, and context limits shared by all attachment paths.

options.title: External plugin capability
options.body: Keep core generic and document the documentExtractors contract so ClawHub plugins provide Office parsers and dependency ownership.

options.title: Provider-native forwarding first
options.body: Defer local Office parsing and make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/91683 the architectural direction for capable providers.

recommendation.title: Shared bounded bundled extraction
recommendation.body: Approve a narrow DOCX-first implementation in the bundled document-extract plugin with strict archive, output, timeout, and context limits shared by all attachment paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent shared media and document-extractor history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the cross-channel product boundary.
